articles.author: Alan West
articles.description:
Traditional Zero Trust was built for humans. A person authenticates, gets a scoped token, makes a few requests per session, and eventually logs out. The security model assumes a user who reads screens, clicks buttons, and operates at human speed.
AI agents don't work like that. An autonomous agent running a multi-step task might hit 40 different APIs, spawn sub-agents, access databases it's never touched before, and do all of it in under a minute. The security model that works for a human clicking through a dashboard completely falls apart when the "user" is an LLM making thousands of decisions per second.
At RSA Conference 2026 on April 1, Cisco unveiled a Zero Trust architecture built specifically for this problem -- real-time policy enforcement and anomaly detection designed for autonom…
articles.title: Cisco Just Built Zero Trust for AI Agents. Here's Why That Matters.

articles.author: Mohammed Maqsood L
articles.description:
This is a submission for the DEV April Fools Challenge
What I Built
If you try to "brew" coffee, the teapot evaluates the "vibes" of your situation, refuses to help (as a teapot should), and writes a custom, algorithmically-generated poem roasting your life choices.
Demo
https://achieving-container-penguin-hampton.trycloudflare.com/view/teapot-agent/
How I Built It
AI Brain: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash for the "Vibe Analysis" and "Poetic Refusal."
Architecture: Built on a modular Fractal Kernel (Node.js) where features are self-discovering "Agents."
Infrastructure: Hosted on GCP Compute Engine (e2-micro) for 24/7 "Always-On" refusal.
Persistence: Local PostgreSQL instance on the VM to track every failed "brew" in a global ledger.
Security: Locked down with Cloudflare Tunnels (obfuscating the origin) and a GCP Firewall that only allows traffic from the Cloudflare edge.
Process Management: Handled by PM2 with systemd auto-restart.
Prize Category
Best Google AI Usage: For using Gemini 2.5 Flash to bring logic and sass to an ancient HTTP status code.
Best Ode to Larry Masinter: I’ve fully implemented the HTCPCP headers (x-vibe-context) and strict 418 status code compliance. Larry would be... well, he'd be something.
articles.title: This is a submission for the DEV April Fools Challenge

If you want a social media agent, you create a social media workspace. If you want an engineering agent, you create an engineering workspace.

The Idea


The fix seemed obvious: Ctrl+V should be context-aware. If I'm in a terminal and I have an image on my clipboard, I probably want the file path, not the image data. If I'm in a text editor, paste normally. If I'm in a browser, paste normally.
The key insight is that the behavior should be invisible. I didn't want a new command to memorize. I wanted Ctrl+V to just do the right thing depending on where I was.
TCP has two layers.
The keyboard layer is an AutoHotkey v2 script that runs in the background as a tray process. It intercepts Ctrl+V at the OS level. When you press it, AHK checks which window is focused. If it's a terminal, it hands off to the Python core. If it's not, it does nothing and lets the normal paste go through.
The Python core handles the logic:

articles.description:
Introduction
Illegal wildlife trade is one of the largest criminal industries in the world, threatening the survival of countless animal species. From exotic pets to animal parts used for profit, millions of animals are captured, transported, and sold under inhumane conditions every year.
This issue not only harms animals but also disrupts ecosystems and contributes to global environmental problems. Understanding the dangers of illegal wildlife trade is essential for protecting biodiversity and ensuring the survival of endangered species.
What Is Illegal Wildlife Trade?
Illegal wildlife trade involves the unlawful capture, transport, and sale of animals or animal products.
This includes:
Exotic pets
Animal skins and fur
Ivory and horns
Traditional medicine ingredients
According to entity["organization","World Wildlife Fund","international conservation organization"], illegal wildlife trade is a major threat to biodiversity worldwide.
Why It Is Dangerous
Threat to Species Survival
Many species are pushed toward extinction due to overexploitation.
Animal Suffering
Animals are often transported in poor conditions, leading to injury or death.
Environmental Impact
Removing species from ecosystems disrupts natural balance.
The Role of Awareness
Raising awareness is one of the most effective ways to combat illegal wildlife trade.
Initiatives like AnimalWatch365 help educate people about the dangers of exploiting wildlife and encourage responsible behavior.
What Can Be Done
Avoid buying wildlife products
Support conservation organizations
Report illegal activities
Spread awareness
Conclusion
Illegal wildlife trade is a serious global issue that requires immediate attention. By taking action and spreading awareness, individuals can help protect animals and preserve ecosystems.
articles.title: The Hidden Dangers of Illegal Wildlife Trade and Why It Must Be Stopped
